title: Least Squares: Project, Don't Solve
topic: When a linear system Ax = b has no solution because b is not in the column space, the next best thing is to project b onto the column space and solve for the result. That gives the normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb. Visualised as fitting a line through three noisy points: the line tilts to minimise the sum of squared vertical residuals, and the minimum lands at exactly the line whose error vector is perpendicular to the column space of A.

beats.narration: Three points won't all lie on one line. What's the best you can do?

elements.content: Three points won't all lie on one line — what's the best fit?

beats.narration: Three noisy data points. We want a line through them. Two unknowns, slope and intercept — but three equations. The system is overdetermined, so no line passes through all three.

elements.content: Three data points (1,1.4), (2,1.9), (3,3.3) on a small grid
Two candidate lines that each miss at least one point

beats.narration: So pick the line that minimises the sum of squared vertical residuals. Tilt the slope back and forth; the squared-error total rises and falls. The best fit is the slope where it bottoms out.

elements.content: Three data points (fixed), a line of varying slope tilting from steep to shallow
elements.note: drive slope by useSprite localTime — sweep over ~12s

elements.content: Three vertical residual line segments from each data point to the candidate line
Three small squares whose side equals the residual length (the 'squared error' literally drawn)

beats.narration: There's a closed-form recipe. The error vector b minus A x has to be perpendicular to every column of A. Multiply both sides by A transpose, and you get the normal equations A transpose A x equals A transpose b. Solve those once, and you're done.

elements.content: Residual must be perpendicular to the column space — that's the projection.

beats.narration: When there is no exact answer, project. The same trick that found the closest point on a line works for the closest point in the column space.

elements.content: Closest point in the column space — same trick, bigger stage.
